claims: The International Space Station (ISS) is a habitable artificial satellite.
The ISS is a microgravity laboratory.
The ISS orbits Earth approximately 250 miles (400 km) up.
The ISS orbits at 17,500 mph.
The ISS has been orbiting Earth since 1998.
The ISS is a multi-nation collaboration.
The ISS is about the size of a football field.
The primary purpose of the ISS is to serve as a research laboratory in low-Earth orbit for experiments in biology, physics, astronomy, and medicine.
The ISS typically hosts a crew of six or seven.
The ISS has held up to 13 people during crew handovers.
Assembly of the ISS began in 1998.
Assembly of the ISS required over 40 missions.
Assembly of the ISS required over 221 spacewalks.
The Russian Orbital Segment (ROS) and the U.S. Orbital Segment (USOS).
The ISS serves as a testing ground for space manufacturing and technological innovations.
The ISS has a scheduled deorbit planned for 2031.
The ISS orbits Earth 16 times a day.
The ISS appears as a fast-moving, bright star.
The ISS is usually best seen around sunrise or sunset.
The ISS offers roughly the same living space as a six-bedroom house.
The ISS includes the Destiny lab from the U.S.
The ISS includes the Kibō lab from Japan.
The ISS includes the Columbus lab from Europe.
The ISS features seven sleeping quarters.
The ISS features two bathrooms.
The ISS features a gym.
The ISS features the 360-degree viewing Cupola.
The solar panels of the ISS cover approximately one acre.
Water on the ISS is recycled from urine and breath.
Oxygen on the ISS is generated through electrolysis.
